prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind O&M; scope: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs, electrical up to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: boundary, dispatch, authorized signals, status; produces Export Limit Advisory when export capability < dispatch target; applies accepted export ceiling, records effective time. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): executes authorized control, limits output, blocks protection-conflicting commands, safe mode on auxiliary loss; produces Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor feed Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur): Leading Edge Tile Image; repeats pass if coverage insufficient; Blade Specialist reviews. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; sends Transformer Tap Snapshot (Shore Control Room checks tap in export reviews); mode Substation Degraded (restrictions communicated). Substation Operator: limits, rounds, switching only by authorized personnel with approved instructions, identity confirmation, clearances, affected parties informed; on protection alarm/abnormal/monitoring loss limits switching, escalates; notifies Grid Dispatcher of export-affecting conditions; status updates to Shore Control Room; shift records. Electrical Technician works under authorization/isolation. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, V/f limits, no unapproved paralleling, sheds loads; Start Test Trace in approved test; failure to start/sustain load→defect. SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale): time-stamped data to Shore Control Room (Amber Quay), measurements of delivered power; produces Session Revocation Receipt, used by Cybersecurity Gateway in access reviews. Shore Control Room keeps dispatch target, ramp rate, review time. Grid Dispatcher issues active-power targets/ramps; priority safety>protection>export. Control Engineer validates data, reviews instructions vs plant status, confirms response within ramp. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): requested vs available capability; Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint: record scope, start, review point. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master; permits. Crew Transfer Vessel: Harness Audit Card. Weather Analyst: Wave Burst Record. Port Agent: Berth Slot Confirmation. Redoubt (permit control) blocks release until

New part:
S377: Turbine Controller adjusts output in accordance with validated plant commands and local equipment protections.
S378: Converter Cabinet status is reviewed for alarms or restrictions that could affect export capability.
S379: Offshore Substation operating status is included in the assessment of the available export path.
S380: Main Transformer loading is monitored against its approved continuous and short-term limits.
S381: Export Cable Monitor indications are checked for conditions that require a reduced transfer level.
S382: Substation Operator coordinates switching activity that could alter the available export configuration.
S383: Grid Dispatcher is notified when measured delivery differs materially from the instructed target or when an operating limit is approached.
S384: Control Engineer records the reason for any temporary deviation from the requested output and the action taken.
S385: Fleet Dispatch Console retains the instruction history and the corresponding plant response for later review.
S386: If communications with the grid are interrupted, the Shore Control Room maintains the last validated operating limit while seeking clarification through the approved channel.
S387: Emergency Generator operation is not treated as a means of maintaining export unless the approved electrical configuration explicitly supports it.
S388: Duty Planner considers active dispatch constraints when scheduling work that would reduce generation or access to export equipment.
S389: Shift records capture dispatch instructions, constraint decisions, measured response, and unresolved follow-up actions.
S390: Vessel Master produces the Crew Count Correction when a verified headcount differs from the departure record.
S391: Crew accountability covers personnel movement between shore facilities, vessels, offshore structures, and the return journey.
S392: Personnel Tracking Console maintains the current accountability status for personnel assigned to offshore work.
S393: Personnel confirm their identity before entering controlled shore access areas.
S394: North Access Scanner records identity checks at the north shore access point.
S395: South Access Scanner records identity checks at the south shore access point.
S396: Duty Planner verifies that planned crew assignments match the approved work schedule before mobilization.
S397: Marine Coordinator reviews the intended crew movement against vessel capacity and operating conditions.
S398: Vessel Master confirms the departure roster before the vessel leaves port.
S399: The departure headcount is reconciled against the crew manifest before the vessel gets underway.
S400: Marine Coordinator monitors reported vessel movements during transit to offshore locations.
S401: Vessel AIS Receiver provides vessel position information for movement monitoring.
S402: Personnel report any change in destination or transfer plan to the Vessel Master as soon as practicable.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
